drills.q: Your multi-stage build's final image is still large. What are the two most likely culprits?
drills.a: 1) COPY --from=builder is copying more than the compiled artifact (whole /build dir including source/object files instead of just the installed package/binary). 2) The final base image itself isn't minimal (not -slim/distroless), still carrying unnecessary OS weight.

drills.q: A teammate removes a leaked secret with RUN rm /tmp/secret.txt in a later Dockerfile layer and calls it fixed. Are they right?
drills.a: No -- the earlier layer containing the secret is still part of the image's immutable layer history and can be extracted directly from the image tarball or via docker history --no-trunc, regardless of later instructions.

drills.q: You add a BuildKit cache mount for pip but CI build times don't improve. Why might that be?
drills.a: Many CI providers run each build in an ephemeral environment where BuildKit's local cache mount storage doesn't persist across runs unless configured with a persistent volume or the CI system's own layer-cache feature -- a cache mount only helps across builds sharing the same builder/cache storage.

drills.q: A debug sidecar sharing --pid=container:X can see the target's processes but can't read files under /proc/<pid>/fd. Why, and what's the fix?
drills.a: Sharing the PID namespace doesn't grant filesystem/mount namespace access. Fix: also share the mount and net namespaces, or use nsenter --target <pid> --mount --net --pid from a privileged debug container to enter all relevant namespaces at once.

drills.q: Give a concrete production symptom of the Alpine musl libc vs Debian glibc incompatibility risk.
drills.a: Intermittent or environment-specific DNS resolution failures for hostnames that resolve fine outside the container (musl's resolver handles certain nsswitch/multi-A-record scenarios differently), or a native extension segfaulting only on the Alpine-based image despite identical source and dependency versions on Debian.

drills.q: You've correctly ordered manifest-copy before source-copy, but the build context upload itself takes 20 seconds every build. What's missing?
drills.a: A .dockerignore file. Without one, the entire build context (.git history, venvs, node_modules, build artifacts) gets tarred and sent to the daemon before any cache lookup happens, regardless of cache hits later in the Dockerfile.

drills.q: Does docker history on your final shipped image reveal a secret used only in a discarded intermediate builder stage?
drills.a: No -- docker history on the tagged final image only shows that image's own layer chain. The risk is in the build cache, CI logs, and any --cache-to registry target that might retain the builder stage's layers separately, not in the final image's own history.

drills.q: Your Dockerfile has three stages and BuildKit's parallel execution isn't speeding anything up. Why?
drills.a: Check whether the stages are genuinely independent in the dependency graph, or whether each FROM <previous-stage>/COPY --from=<previous-stage> creates a strictly linear chain -- parallelism requires sibling stages, not a chain relabeled as multiple FROM lines.

drills.q: Explain the mechanical reason ordering matters: why does copying requirements.txt separately from source code speed up builds?
drills.a: COPY layers are cache-keyed on the content of exactly the files copied. Copying only the manifest first keeps that layer (and the potentially multi-minute install layer after it) cached when only source changes; copying everything together invalidates the install layer on any file change anywhere in the context.

drills.q: Your app needs to bind port 80 but you want to avoid running as root. Two valid approaches?
drills.a: Grant the specific Linux capability (--cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE with --cap-drop=ALL, non-root USER), or avoid the problem entirely by binding a high port (8080) inside the container and mapping it to 80 at the host/load-balancer layer.
